summary: The association lists a Garrett County Negro Mountain tower as gone; no source read gives its build date, staffing or removal.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association. No source read gives a removal date or describes the site today.

evidence.supports: Negro Mountain is a long ridge running about 30 miles from Deep Creek Lake in Maryland north to the Casselman River in Pennsylvania
evidence.quote: Negro Mountain is a long ridge of the Allegheny Mountains in the eastern United States, stretching 30-mile (48 km) from Deep Creek Lake in Maryland north to the Casselman River in Pennsylvania

evidence.supports: association lists the Negro Mountain tower in Garrett County as gone
Scharf 1882 account reprinted by the Garrett County Historical Society
evidence.quote: This is the story of how Negro Mountain in Garrett County received its names as told in Thomas Scharf's 1882 History of Western Maryland

evidence.supports: Col. Thomas Cresap led the pursuit in the Scharf account
evidence.quote: COL. THOMAS CRESAP made his home at Skipton or Shawnee Oldtown on the Potomac.
His body-servant, Nemesis, a big negro, was cleaning his gun

evidence.supports: Scharf: the settlement was attacked before the pursuit
evidence.quote: One night the settlement was attacked by Indians

evidence.supports: Scharf: Cresap ordered his men to pursue the attackers
evidence.quote: Col. Cresap ordered his men to prepare to pursue the fleeing savages.

evidence.supports: in the Scharf account Nemesis was slain and buried on the mountain
evidence.quote: Nemesis was slain and buried on the mountain

evidence.supports: Zumbrun research (as reported on the page): the 1756 event; the name Nemesis not in writing until over 120 years after it
evidence.quote: did not appear in writings until after over 120 years from the 1756 event on the mountain

evidence.supports: Zumbrun research indicates Nemesis was a free Black man (source: 'free Negro')
name Negro Mountain appears on maps from 1822
evidence.quote: first appears on maps dating as far back as 1822

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The only tower evidence is the association list (Garrett County, Gone, coordinates) and an empty county heading on the Forest Lookouts page. A search summary said a DNR fire tower list dates a Negro Mountain tower to the mid-1930s at 90 feet, but no page I could read confirms that, so it is left out. The DNR Fire Tower Report (April 2007, towers managed as of December 2006) does not list Negro Mountain, which only shows it was not DNR-managed in 2006. The story spends most of its words on the place name, which is sourced; cut it if the editor wants only tower facts, and the story will then be under the 120-word floor. Web searches used: 2 (cap 2). Pages read: about 4 (Wikipedia, WHILBR, FFLA list, Forest Lookouts page).
